new_statements.quote: Como un parámetro comparativo se tomará de referencia la tonía de la vocal de la sílaba que precede a la vocal de la sílaba modificada. Esto permitirá determinar si la tonía asciende, desciende o mantiene un nivel, teniendo en cuenta que la acentuación en las palabras de la lengua tsotsil recae en la sílaba final.
new_statements.translation: As a comparative parameter, the pitch of the vowel of the syllable preceding the vowel of the modified syllable will be taken as reference. This will make it possible to determine whether the pitch rises, falls or stays level, bearing in mind that stress in the words of the Tsotsil language falls on the final syllable.
new_statements.citation: López Jiménez, José Alfredo. 2010. Estructura, actuación y multimodalidad en la narrativa personal oral (lo'il a'yej) de la comunidad tsotsil de Romerillo, Chamula, Chiapas. Tesis de maestría en Lingüística Indoamericana, CIESAS, México (director: Lourdes de León Pasquel).
new_statements.locator: Chapter 4 'Modificación prosódica en la narrativa tsotsil de Romerillo', p. 116 (PDF page 116), point (a)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (236 pp..) and ran extracted text: PDF page 116 = printed folio 116, ch. 4 preamble, point (a) reads exactly "Como un parámetro comparativo se tomará de referencia la tonía de la vocal de la sílaba que precede a la vocal de la sílaba modificada. Esto permitirá determinar si la tonía asciende, desciende o mantiene un nivel, teniendo en cuenta que la acentuación en las palabras de la lengua tsotsil recae en la sílaba final." Verbatim match with the reported quote (line 4116-4119 of the). Surrounding section (pp. 115-116) sets out the PRAAT method for measuring prosodic modification (duration, pitch, glottal state) in Romerillo narratives; the stress clause is a methodological aside, no…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the last syllable of the word (stated as a general property of Tsotsil by a Chamula-community study; the pan-Tsotsil INALI 2011 writing norm, p. 106, says the same: 'la lengua tsotsil tiene acento prosódico en la última sílaba', with Spanish loans re-stressed finally, Pala > Palá, Mula > Mulá). Note that the Zinacantán descriptions held by the project (Laughlin 1975:23; Haviland 1981:14) distinguish final stress in isolation from root-initial word stress plus phrase-final prominence in connected speech; neither Chamula source makes that distinction.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the Chamula source or the INALI norm. (Laughlin 1975:23, Zinacantán, excepts affective verbs in -luh, 1pl-exclusive suffixed forms and reduplicated disyllabic stems, where stress is non-final.)
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('las palabras'), used as the baseline for a PRAAT pitch analysis of narrative speech; the INALI examples are citation forms of loanwords. Phrase-level stress is not discussed in either Chamula-relevant source.
new_statements.identity_note: tzot1262 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for the retired ISO code tzc 'Chamula Tzotzil', merged into Tzotzil [tzo] (Glottolog tzot1259) in 2009 (CR 2008-061, opened and read). No dedicated linguistic description of the Chamula dialect exists among sources found; the quoted statement comes from a CIESAS MA thesis on the Chamula community of Romerillo (Chamula municipality) that states final word stress as a general Tsotsil property. The corroborating INALI 2011 norm is pan-Tsotsil. The fuller Tzotzil stress descriptions held by the project (Laughlin 1975:23, Haviland 1981:14) are for Zinacantán (tzot1264).

new_statements.quote: En cambio, tsòtsíl lleva un tono alto en la segunda sílaba, reflejando la acentuación final de tsotsil tanto en español como en tsotsil de Chamula; esto muestra que es un préstamo reciente. [p. 40] || Fuera del yucateco, uspanteko y mocho', que han desarrollado tonos léxicos, las lenguas mayas, incluyendo el tseltal y tsotsil en general, no presentan prosodia contrastiva a nivel de palabra: ni acento tónico contrastivo como el del español, ni tonos (Bennett 2016; England & Baird 2017). En Carranza, las palabras se distinguen según el tono de su sílaba inicial, mientras que las sílabas siguientes reciben un tono predecible, con la excepción de ciertos sufijos. [pp. 11-12]
new_statements.translation: By contrast, tsòtsíl carries a high tone on the second syllable, reflecting the final stress of 'tsotsil' both in Spanish and in Chamula Tsotsil; this shows that it is a recent loan. [p. 40] || Apart from Yucatec, Uspanteko and Mocho', which have developed lexical tones, the Mayan languages, including Tseltal and Tsotsil in general, show no contrastive word-level prosody: neither contrastive stress like that of Spanish, nor tones (Bennett 2016; England & Baird 2017). In Carranza, words are distinguished by the tone of their initial syllable, while the following syllables receive a predictable tone, with the exception of certain suffixes. [pp. 11-12]
new_statements.citation: Polian, Gilles. 2017. Tseltal and Tsotsil. In Judith Aissen, Nora England & Roberto Zavala (eds.), The Mayan Languages, 610-647. London: Routledge.
new_statements.locator: Polian 2024, p. 40 (§9 on the glottonyms tseltal/tsotsil; printed folio = PDF page 40); supporting passage p. 11 (§5 'Tonos', PDF page 11) and fn. 6 p. 19.
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: text layer. extracted text gives the p. 40 sentence exactly as quoted ('En cambio, tsòtsíl lleva un tono alto en la segunda sílaba, reflejando la acentuación final de tsotsil tanto en español como en tsotsil de Chamula; esto muestra que es un préstamo reciente.'), printed folio 40 = PDF page 40 (running header checked). The §5 'Tonos' passage is verbatim across PDF pages 11-12 (folios 11-12), as quoted. Minor difference: the supporting footnote 6 ('la última sílaba se representa sin tono, reflejando que en esta sílaba la prosodia frasal remplaza al tono subyacente') is on PDF page 26 = printed folio 26, not p. 19 as the reader stated; content as described. Identity: confirms the the Harvard…
new_statements.relation_note: The Chamula sentence on p. 40 states final stress for Chamula Tsotsil explicitly, matching the existing statement (López Jiménez 2010:116, 'la acentuación en las palabras de la lengua tsotsil recae en la sílaba final') and INALI 2011:106 already held by the project. It adds that word-level prosody in Tsotsil generally is non-contrastive (with Bennett 2016 and England & Baird 2017 cited). CAUTION for the site: this quote is from Polian 2024 (CLECM 11, e319), NOT from the listed Polian 2017 Routledge chapter; the the Harvard library catalogue open_url is a DOAJ record for the 2024 article. Polian 2017 itself was not obtained: doi.org -> taylorfrancis.com returned a not reachable by automated…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Chamula Tsotzil word stress falls on the final syllable (the word 'tsotsil' is stressed finally in Chamula Tsotsil, which is why the Carranza borrowing tsòtsíl carries its high tone on the second syllable). Word stress in Tsotsil generally is non-contrastive (no minimal pairs); the Venustiano Carranza variety is the exception, having developed lexical high/low tone on the initial syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Chamula. The paper's own subject, Venustiano Carranza Tsotsil, is described as tonal (H/L on the initial syllable, minimal pairs in Tables 4-5, pp. 12-13; monosyllabic pairs too), so it does not have a stress system of the Chamula type; fn. 6 (p. 19) notes that the phrase-final syllable carries phrasal prosody in place of its underlying tone.
new_statements.identity_note: The only listed work's open_url does not lead to Polian 2017 'Tseltal and Tsotsil' but to Polian 2024, an article on the Venustiano Carranza (southern) variety of Tsotsil, which is tonal. Its statement about Chamula is a single explicit aside on p. 40 ('la acentuación final de tsotsil.. en tsotsil de Chamula'), which is exactly the variety of item tzot1262. Its general claim (pp. 11-12) is about Tseltal and Tsotsil as a whole: no contrastive word-level stress or tone outside Carranza.
